reason: E2 shows that Pt on a high-entropy oxide resists sintering and maintains CO oxidation activity over 338 h and under moisture cycling, supporting the sintering-suppression and durability premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that a thermal post-treatment of a near-equiatomic alloy forms a nanoporous high-entropy oxide layer, nor that such a layer lowers light-off temperature or resists NO poisoning; E1 only addresses spinel oxides from molecular precursors, not alloy-derived layers.
premises: High configurational entropy in oxides suppresses metal sintering
Nanoporous high-entropy oxide layer can be formed by thermal post-treatment in oxidizing/humid atmosphere
Such an oxide layer lowers CO/hydrocarbon oxidation light-off temperature
The oxide layer enhances resistance to H2O and NO poisoning
The oxide layer provides long-term durability under automotive aging conditions
